source.title: Scaling Laws for Collapse in Asynchronous GRPO
source.authors: Jing-Wei Song; Hao-Feng Xu; Jie Xiao; Cheng-Ke Bao; Jing-Wei Shi; Peng-Bin Feng; Yu-Hang Han; Wei-Xun Wang; Eric Yang; Tian-Yu Shi

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. It is a preprint; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests training stability and collapse timing in asynchronous GRPO on Llama and Qwen language models, a new model and training setting relative to the listed versions. Its own sweeps report training-reward outcomes under varied synchronization intervals and learning rates.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training reward, validation accuracy, collapse times, and gradient cosine. Rows below capture the separately reported model × recipe × condition × measure outcomes bearing on the versions. Cited prior-work results are not included.
record.test_reason: The study measures reward collapse during asynchronous GRPO post-training of language models. None of V1–V6 describes this outcome and setting. In particular, it does not measure curvature, the initial linearized stability limit, recovery above that limit, or edge-of-stability dynamics required by V5. It discusses edge-of-stability literature but does not test or use that finding.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors distinguish an approximately constant-Sη finite-horizon stability boundary from an inverse-learning-rate collapse clock among unstable Llama runs. Qwen3 checks timing only at fixed S with a different budget. They recommend joint calibration and validation over the intended horizon; their proposed drift mechanism remains conditional rather than experimentally established.
record.recipe_differences: Asynchronous vanilla GRPO reinforcement-learning post-training with periodic weight synchronization on language models; not the supervised gradient-training recipes or network interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Collapse and stability outcomes vary with synchronization interval S and learning rate η. At fixed S = 32, lowering η from 10−7 to 8 × 10−8 changes observed collapse to extended-horizon survival. Collapse-time constant differs between Llama and Qwen3 settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Both Llama sizes have identical finite-horizon stability patterns: the main grid separates survival at Sη≤1.6×10−6 from collapse at Sη≥3.2×10−6. Among collapsing configurations only, reported times satisfy t_obsη=3.2×10−5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested asynchronous vanilla-GRPO Llama recipes, synchronization interval and learning rate jointly delimit finite-horizon reward stability; collapsing runs share an approximately inverse-learning-rate clock across tested synchronization intervals.

fits_no_version.finding: At S=32, Llama-3.2-3B survives approximately 1,400 updates at four rates from 5×10−8 to 8×10−8; all three tested seeds survive 500 updates. The latter exceeds the reference clock only at the two higher rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lowering learning rate can produce survival beyond the unstable-regime reference clock in this asynchronous GRPO setup, rather than merely delaying collapse according to that clock.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen3-8B at S=16 collapses at 64, 128, and 320 updates for the three larger rates, giving t_obsη=6.4×10−5; η=10−7 survives approximately 800 updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inverse-learning-rate collapse timing also appears in the tested Qwen3 model–data setting at one synchronization interval, with a different fitted budget; invariance across synchronization intervals is untested there.

record.problems: The main sweeps use one seed per configuration; three-seed checks cover only Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct at S = 32. Stable means no observed collapse within the finite training horizon, not proof of indefinite stability. The experimental models are language models trained with GRPO on math data, and collapse is defined through verifier reward rather than classification error. Table 1 is flattened in the supplied text, obscuring cell assignments for some entries; prose and other described values resolve the main qualitative boundary, but not every apparent table cell.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out for the stated results. Some Table 1 cells are flattened and cannot be assigned to individual synchronization conditions; those ambiguous values are not reconstructed as condition-specific rows.

untested.parts: All: convolutional networks trained from random initialization, CIFAR training classification error, corrupted labels, and capacity or regularization qualifications.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
All: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified plain or residual training exceptions.
All: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.

All: recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, sharpness at the stability threshold, and divergence relative to that threshold. Runs stop after collapse is identified, so post-collapse recovery is also untested.
All: batch-normalization effects on speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6, not judgments that the reported GRPO outcomes are unreadable. Sections 4.2–4.3 resolve collapse-time assignments despite the flattened table: 160 updates applies only to collapsing S=16 and 32 configurations at 2×10−7, and 320 updates only to S=32 at 10−7. The record's claim that ambiguous assignments were not reconstructed contradicts its erroneous timing rows. No additional results bearing on V1–V6 were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No tests of random-initialization supervised gradient training, classification error, CIFAR benchmarks, label corruption, or model width.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments, spurious-minimum outcomes, or neuron-count comparisons.
No plain versus residual network depth comparison, identity shortcut intervention, or normalization-free residual training test.
No initialization comparison or plain-network depth and trainability sweep.
No learning-rate-above-stability-limit test of the stated loss-curvature mechanism; the paper varies learning rate in asynchronous RL and defines collapse by reward drop.
No batch-normalization comparison or normalization intervention.
